newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia to use English test to limit immigrants.
newsitem.headline: Australia to use English test to limit immigrants.

text.p: Australia will introduce an English language test in 1997 to restrict its family reunion immigrant intake.
The Australian government late on Friday night announced a series of administrative measures, including the language test, to restrict certain types of immigration.

The language test from July would be used for non-dependent children, brothers, sisters and working-age parents, but not closer family members such as spouses. The number of occupations requiring vocational English would also be expanded.

"This means, for example, that most young and skilled applicants with no English but fluency in two or more languages will no longer be successful," Immigration Minister Philip Ruddock told parliament.
Other measures to restrict immigration include giving priority to people whose sponsors are Australian citizens and capping the immigrant intake at 74,000 in 1996/1997.
Immigrant groups on Saturday condemned the changes, claiming they resembled the old White Australia immigration policy.
Australia's discriminatory White Australia immigration policy, which required immigrants to pass an English dictation test, was abandoned in the 1960s.

But Ruddock said the tighter immigrant rules were necessary because the immigration programme was out of balance and out of control, with family immigration accounting for about 70 percent of immigrants, the spouse category growing by 32 percent, and the parent category by more than 74 percent.

He also said the rules were required to stamp out fraud and restore public confidence in the immigration programme as entry standards had been reduced and reports of sham marriages had become commonplace.

But opposition Labor immigration spokesman Duncan Kerr said the government's proposals to allow more independent immigrants into Australia at the expense of family reunion applicants at a time of high unemployment was madness.
Australia's unemployment level is currently 8.5 percent.

"Keeping Australian families separated and bringing in people with no ties to Australia to try and take their jobs is not the way to restore confidence in the migration programme," Kerr said in a statement.
